suggestions.assertion: Finds at least 3 instances of incorrect 'Claude in Excel' usage
suggestions.reason: This assertion checks quantity but not precision. An overzealous auditor that also flags the legitimate line 70 cross-reference would still pass (3+ instances found) but would demonstrate poor judgment. Consider adding an assertion like 'Does NOT flag the line 70 YAML cross-reference as a defect' to test discriminating judgment. The current run happened to get this right, but the assertion doesn't verify it.

No assertion checks whether the recommended replacements are correct (e.g., D6-4 should match the exact cowork-content.md canonical pattern). An auditor that flags the right lines but suggests wrong replacements (e.g., 'Claude Cowork' instead of 'Cowork') would pass all current assertions. Consider: 'At least one recommended fix quotes the canonical cowork-content.md pattern verbatim.'

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover the key dimensions well — detection, classification, recommendation direction, taxonomy structure, and false-positive avoidance. The two suggestions above would tighten precision checking: discriminating judgment on borderline cases, and correctness of recommended fixes (not just their existence).
